mistakes.what: Assumed container would restart from --rebuild ansible flag
mistakes.revealed: The ansible docker_compose_v2 state: absent with ignore_errors: yes was silently failing
mistakes.corrected: Added explicit 'docker compose down' command and recreate: always option

mistakes.what: Used wrong field name for invite code in Hooks.php - wpInviteCode instead of wpinviteCode
mistakes.revealed: EntityAttestation pages weren't being created because invite code wasn't being found
mistakes.corrected: Updated Hooks.php to check multiple field name variations

mistakes.what: Initial system user creation didn't safeguard against account squatting
mistakes.revealed: Used 'steal: true' which could hijack existing accounts
mistakes.corrected: Changed to 'steal: false' and added system user creation during update.php

mistakes.what: Initially thought recreate option for docker_compose_v2 accepted 'smart' value
mistakes.revealed: Ansible module documentation misread; only accepts 'always', 'never', or 'auto'
mistakes.corrected: Changed to 'auto' value which works correctly

mistakes.what: Used wrong hook interface name - MediaWiki\Hook\LocalUserCreatedHook instead of MediaWiki\Auth\Hook\LocalUserCreatedHook
mistakes.revealed: Hook interface didn't exist in MediaWiki 1.43 compatibility
mistakes.corrected: Updated import path to correct namespace

For unified attestations, make invite record just be a different kind of attestation at User:X/Attestations/invite-record rather than EntityAttestation
Question about inconsistent path formats - why EntityAttestation vs Attestations/by-X? Prefers unified structure
Casual communication style preferred ('lil bubba' greeting), specific UI changes for EPK

philosophy.summary: Deployment should work from automation untouched; manual fixes violate operational integrity
philosophy.quote: Totally right - the no-touch policy exists for good reason. The deploy should handle this.

philosophy.summary: System design should handle edge cases at the architecture level, not through manual intervention
philosophy.quote: The ansible playbook's docker_compose_v2 with state: absent and ignore_errors: yes - the container restart issue was a design problem

philosophy.summary: Initial invite attestation is foundational trust proof; optional musician web-of-trust via rabbithole comes later
philosophy.quote: The invitation system handles accountability for accounts, and the musician web-of-trust via rabbithole is a separate layer that can build on top of it later

philosophy.summary: Subpages provide clearer ownership - each attestation author visible in URL
philosophy.quote: Each attestation is clearly owned by its author (the URL tells you: User:Alice/Attestations/by-JMyles); revocation is clean: delete the subpage

portrait: This slice captures magent building out the account-creation and web-of-trust infrastructure for PickiPedia, working closely with Justin on design decisions. It's methodical infrastructure work: fixing deployment issues (docker-compose recreation semantics), debugging field naming conventions in MediaWiki forms, and designing the initial structure for a trustworthy account system. The work moves from the immediate problem (container not restarting) through larger architectural questions (should attestations be separate pages or unified? where should users see them?) toward a working system that lets any user vouch for any other. Justin steers toward simplicity and correctness over features; magent implements carefully, tests thoroughly, and adjusts the design when unified paths make more sense than parallel structures. The tone is collaborative - magent explains trade-offs clearly enough that Justin can make good design calls, and Skyler joins toward the end with EPK polish work done in the same direct style.
